_comment: Peerlark Optics 'The North Star isn't the brightest' cosmic-mythology-voiceover reel (Peerlark is a made-up beginner-telescope brand) — THE WORKED EXAMPLE. Copy to config.json and edit. A ~31s faceless 9:16 reel where a warm contemplative spoken VO reframes the North Star as 'the steady one, not the brightest' over 12 weighted Ken-Burns cuts of cosmic stills, with the hook 'Stop looking for the brightest star.' faded on over the open + Whisper captions. Pipeline: (1) lock the VO (ElevenLabs eleven_v3 tone-tagged, atempo-clamped 1.25 -> 31.4s — the delivered duration sets the timeline); (2) 6 Flux Pro 1.1 cosmic stills in ONE indigo+gold look (reused to 12 cuts); (3) FREE assembly — weighted beat-sync (cut_dur = VO_dur * weight / Sum(weights)), Ken-Burns per still, ffmpeg concat + VO composite (crf18) + hook alpha-fade overlay + VEED/Whisper caption burn. Master 1080x1920 h264+aac, ~31.4s (12 cuts). See scripts/PIPELINE.md for the step map. Creative fields -- vo.script, vo.tone_tags, vo.voice_id/voice_settings, hook.text, look_pack (name, style_descriptor, palette_anchors), shots[].prompt and the sequence weights -- come from the recipe's choices (story shape, narrator, voice, tone, visual world, art style); never copy them as defaults. Copy the structure and field names only.
title: The North Star isn't the brightest

vo._comment: Locked FIRST — the delivered, atempo-stretched VO duration sets the timeline. Rendered 39.24s at eleven_v3; a 23s target needed atempo 1.71, CLAMPED at 1.25 -> 31.4s final (manifest flagged 'atempo_clamped' + 'duration_overshoot' rather than chipmunking the voice). The demo's first draft used eleven_multilingual_v2 + the Lauren voice (l4Coq6695JDX9xtLqXDE); v2 used eleven_v3 with the tone-tagged script.
vo.script: [soft, casual] Okay… can I tell you a secret about the North Star? Everyone assumes it's the brightest star up there — but it's not even close. Polaris isn't here to dazzle you — it's here to stay put. While every other star wheels across the night, it barely moves… the one fixed point in the whole sky. Sailors, hikers, runaways? They didn't follow the loudest light… they followed the steady one. It doesn't need to shine the most. It just needs to show up. So next time you feel lost… look north.
vo.tone_tags: [soft, casual] opener; warm, contemplative, unhurried delivery
vo._note_atempo: atempo_clamped: rendered 39.24s vs target 23.00s would require factor 1.706, clamped at 1.25. The reel runs 31.4s rather than chipmunk the voice — consider trimming the script if a tighter cut is required.

hook._comment: The ONE on-screen reframe line, faded on over the OPEN via ffmpeg drawtext alpha window (in ~0.5s at t=0.3, hold, out ~0.6s ending t=3.0) — never persistent, never a caption, never in-world text on a still.
hook.text: Stop looking for the brightest star.

look_pack._comment: ONE cosmic look baked into EVERY image prompt so all stills read as one film. 'no text, no words' is load-bearing — the reel's only text is the hook + captions, added in post.
look_pack.name: COSMIC_INDIGO_GOLD
look_pack.style_descriptor: cinematic, ethereal, mystical, deep indigo and gold color palette, fine star particles, volumetric light, ultra-detailed, vertical 9:16 composition, no text, no words
palette_anchors: warm gold rings / particles / dawn light (accent)

image_engine._note: Generate at the OUTPUT resolution 1080x1920 (the old 'portrait_16_9' preset returned ~576x1024, soft after the 2x Ken-Burns). gen_images2.py generated 6 hero stills (img5..img10); gen_images.py generated the first 4 (img1..img4). 10 assets total; the sequence reuses a few to reach 12 cuts.

shots.prompt: A single steady white-gold star high above a deep-indigo starfield, calm and certain
A lone silhouette on a cliff under a vast cosmic sky, one bright star directly overhead
Abstract golden star trails circling one fixed point in deep space
Dawn light over a figure walking forward, one faint star still visible above them — 'look north'
The whole night sky wheeling in long gold arcs around one unmoving star, vast and patient
A small wooden boat on a dark sea under a vast glowing starfield, one star guiding its bow, dramatic
Flaring comets and bright streaks rushing past a calm silhouetted figure who keeps looking up at one quiet star
Dramatic wide view of golden star trails sweeping across the sky, fine particles catching light
A solitary figure standing tall in warm golden starlight, steady and unshaken
One brilliant star burning alone in a deep-indigo cosmos, soft nebula drifting around it, quiet hope

sequence._comment: Weighted beat-sync (from build_video2.py's SEQ array): cut_dur = VO_dur * weight / Sum(weights). 12 cuts, ~10 unique stills (img1_polaris + img8_trails2 each reused twice). Heavier weights hold LONGER on the open (1.15) and the dawn 'look north' close (1.2); the setup cuts run shorter (0.8-0.95). Ken-Burns: scale 2x, center crop, zoompan to zoom_end 1.10; zoom_out on the flagged cuts; fade_in 0.4 on the FIRST cut, fade_out 0.6 on the LAST.

captions._comment: VEED/Whisper subtitle burn on working/draft2.mp4 -> finals/northstar-myth-v2.mp4. Tracks the spoken VO. Bottom third, white, mid shadow. The stills carry NO in-world text (the reel's only text is the hook + these captions). Local Whisper + ffmpeg subtitles burn is the free fallback if VEED is locked.

audio_mix._comment: The spoken VO is the full audio bed — there is NO music bed by default. Add a ducked instrumental only if the brief calls for one; then mix it UNDER the VO.

voiceover.note: the spoken eleven_v3 VO IS the spine; no music bed by default

hook.note: the ONE on-screen reframe line, alpha-faded on over the open, never persistent / never in-world

captions.note: VEED/Whisper subtitle burn tracking the VO, bottom, white #FFFFFF

fades.note: fade-in on the first Ken-Burns cut, fade-out on the last
